content.title: Ford recalls more than 1.3 million F-150 trucks because of a transmission problem
content.text: NewsFord has recalled more than 1 million F-150 vehicles from model years 2015-17 because they may unexpectedly downshift into second gear and cause the driver to lose control. (AP file photo) APBy Deb Kiner | dkiner@pennlive.comFord Motor Co. has recalled 1,392,935 F-150 pickup trucks because the transmission can unexpectedly downshift into second gear which could cause the driver to lose control.The recall includes model years 2015-17. Ford said the trucks affected have a 6-speed automatic transmission and were built between March 12, 2014, and August 18, 2017. Ford said the issue happens when the transmission sensor fails to communicate properly with the vehicle’s computer system, according to documents filed with the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.In some cases, Ford said, the driver may notice an illuminated malfunction indicator light or wrench light in the instrument panel.Ford said it is aware of 444 warranty claims, 121 field reports, 105 customer service reports and 316 formal complaints in the United States potentially related to this concern, received between April 24, 2015, and Nov. 3, 2025. Ford is aware of two injuries and one accident potentially related to this issue. Dealers will update the powertrain control module software at no charge.Letters to owners are expected to be mailed April 27. Additional letters will be mailed when a final remedy is available, anticipated to be in July.For more information, owners can call Ford customer service at 866-436-7332.
